name: Meridian Munitions Defender-12 'Alley Cat'
description:
The Meridian Munitions Defender-12 is a pump-action shotgun chambered in 12 gauge with a 14-inch barrel, pistol grip, and a heat shield over the barrel. The weapon is stripped to bare essentials — no stock, no sights beyond a brass bead, no accessory rail. It is a close-range violence delivery system priced for the Shelf market and designed to fit in places where a full-size shotgun won't.

The Alley Cat is the Shelf's answer to the question 'What if I need a shotgun but I live in a one-room apartment?' The pistol grip and short barrel make the weapon compact enough to store in a closet or under a cot, and the heat shield prevents the barrel from burning the user's hand after multiple shots — a detail that suggests Meridian Munitions expects the weapon to be fired more than once in rapid succession.

The weapon's name comes from its prevalence in the narrow service alleys that run behind Shelf apartment blocks — spaces too tight for full-size long arms but too dangerous to traverse unarmed. Security patrols through these alleys carry the Defender-12 in one hand and a flashlight in the other, a configuration that the pistol grip specifically enables. The Alley Cat is a creature of the dark, tight spaces where Shelf life happens behind closed doors.
specifications:
caliber: 12 gauge
effective_range: 15 meters (buckshot)
rate_of_fire: Pump-action
magazine_capacity: 4+1 rounds
weight: 2.5 kg
overall_length: 56 cm
tactical_use: A compact pump shotgun for confined-space operations. The pistol grip enables one-handed carry with a flashlight in the other. The short barrel maximizes spread at close range. Recoil with the pistol grip is harsh — sustained aimed fire is difficult. Best used for close-range ambush defense or patrol in tight environments where a full-size shotgun is impractical.
cultural_context: The Alley Cat is the weapon of the in-between spaces — the alleys, stairwells, maintenance corridors, and utility tunnels that form the circulatory system of Shelf districts. It is not a weapon for open confrontation. It is a weapon for the moment when something appears in a narrow space and there are no good options, only a bad option and a worse one.
story_hooks: An Alley Cat is found propped against a wall in a service tunnel with a note attached: 'For whoever needs this next.' The weapon is loaded and the note is in a dead person's handwriting.

A series of attacks in Shelf maintenance corridors are attributed to someone using an Alley Cat — but the attacker is never seen, and the weapon is never found. The attacks only happen when certain maintenance schedules align.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutally minimalist pump-action shotgun stripped to its functional skeleton. Aggressive forward-swept silhouette dominated by a short, thick barrel with pronounced heat shield. Pistol grip extends downward like a clenched fist. No stock, no rails, no unnecessary geometry—pure violence compressed into a 56cm package.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 56 cm | Barrel length: 14 cm | Height with grip: ~20 cm | Width at receiver: 5 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Dense and front-heavy at 2.5 kg—substantial enough to feel purposeful, light enough for one-handed carry. The weight sits forward in the barrel assembly, creating leverage pressure in the grip.
physical_description.primary_material: Steel receiver and barrel with reinforced aluminum pump mechanism. Polymer furniture on grip and heat shield mounting points.
physical_description.finish: Mil-spec matte black on steel surfaces with functional wear—scuffs and handling marks. Heat shield shows oxidized steel with brushed finish in high-contact areas. Bare aluminum visible at pump rails from repeated cycling.
physical_description.color_scheme: Flat black primary with brushed steel/aluminum accents. Bare brass bead sight glints dully at muzzle. Heat shield slots reveal burnt orange interior from barrel heat.
physical_description.grip_texture: Stippled polymer—aggressive micro-texture for wet-hand retention. Slight contour to cradle palm. Pump handles wrapped in thin rubberized coating, worn smooth at contact points.
distinctive_features: Prominent ribbed barrel heat shield with lateral cooling vents
Brass bead sight soldered directly to barrel—no adjustment, point-and-aim
Exposed pump rod with knurled grip texture
Charging handle positioned for single-handed operation
Magazine tube cap worn shiny from loading
Visible gas tube seams running along top of receiver
Trigger guard sized for gloved operation
Sling loop welded at receiver rear
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: MERIDIAN MUNITIONS stamped in block letters on left receiver flat. Serial number etched below. 'DEFENDER-12' roll-marked on barrel. Gauge marking (12) stamped near magazine tube. Minimal branding—utilitarian manufacturer stamp only.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but maintained. Polymer shows handling scuffs. Steel surfaces exhibit light rust bloom in sheltered areas—typical of Shelf humidity exposure. Heat shield interior blackened from use. Bead sight shows wear marks from aiming. Magazine tube cap shows repeated hand oils and wear polish.
